Principal Polymer Processing Engineer

Injection Molding

Location: Largo, FL (Remote)
Department: Engineering / Operations
Job Category: Engineering
Career Track: Individual Contributor
Job Profile: Principal Engineer
Reports To: Sr. Director Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
FLSA Status: Exempt

***This position is not eligible for employer-based sponsorship***


Position Summary

The Principal Polymer Processing Engineer is a recognized technical expert responsible for advancing injection molding capabilities, polymer processing technologies, and manufacturing performance across CONMED. This role provides technical leadership for the plastic parts design geometry for injection molding manufacturability; for new injection molds design conceptualization, manufacturing and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding cell equipment selection and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding process optimization and qualification; and for the sustaining support of the plastic injection molding process and mold’s production life cycle maintenance for plastic parts used to manufacture medical devices and components. Working across Engineering, Operations, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and external partners, the Principal Polymer Processing Engineer leads highly complex technical initiatives from concept through commercialization and ongoing production. The individual serves as a trusted technical advisor, applying advanced engineering judgment to solve critical processing challenges; establishing technical standards; reducing manufacturing risk; and improving product quality, cost, capacity and reliability.


This is an individual-contributor position that leads through technical expertise, influence, and cross-functional collaboration rather than direct people management.


Key Responsibilities


Technical Leadership and Process Development

  • Serve as a Technical Advisor to Sourcing and Quality in custom molders facilities; molding cells equipment; injection molding process optimization and troubleshooting; mold design and manufacturing; mold preventive maintenance, troubleshooting and tooling engineering; metrology and MSA; and quality engineering technical capacities & capabilities assessment, and periodic audits.
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert in part design conceptualization for injection molding manufacturability; injection molding process optimization; injection molding process engineering (troubleshooting); mold design concept optimization; and mold tooling engineering (troubleshooting).
  • Lead the development, optimization, qualification and validation of complex injection molding processes, equipment, molds and supporting technologies.
  • Establish robust processing strategies based on polymer science, material characteristics, part design, mold design, equipment capability, and intended product requirements.
  • Apply scientific molding principles and structured experimentation to define processing windows and ensure repeatable, capable, and controlled manufacturing processes.
  • Provide technical direction for challenging molding applications involving tight tolerances, complex geometries, engineered resins, high-performance polymers, multi-material components, insert molding, overmolding, or other specialized processes.
  • Evaluate emerging polymer-processing technologies and recommend investments that support product innovation, manufacturing capability, capacity, quality, and long-term business needs.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, engineering practices, design guidelines, specifications, and process-development methodologies.
  • Translate complex technical information into clear recommendations for engineering, operations, and business leadership.

New Product and Technology Development

  • Partner with R&D, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, Operations, and Supply Chain to support new product development and product-transfer activities.
  • Provide design-for-manufacturability guidance related to polymer selection, molded-part design geometry, tooling strategy, tolerances, gating, cooling, shrinkage, warpage, and process capability.
  • Lead or provide technical oversight for mold-flow analysis; tool design reviews; mold manufacturing and performance testing; process characterization; equipment selection and performance testing; and manufacturing-readiness assessments.
  • Identify technical risks early in the development process and establish appropriate mitigation plans.
  • Lead the transition of injection-molded products and processes from development through validation, commercialization, and sustained production.
  • Define critical process parameters and support the development of appropriate inspection, monitoring, and control strategies.
  • Ensure that technical decisions balance product performance, patient and user needs, compliance, manufacturability, cost, capacity, and business continuity.

Process Validation and Compliance

  • Provide technical leadership for mold bench assembly and functional performance assessment; mold installation qualification; molding cell equipment assessment and performance testing; mold dry cycling, mold first out-of-tool and mold functional performance testing; molding process characterization and optimization; plastic forming steel compliance assessment and, if applicable, tweaking (grooming); mold operational qualification; and mold performance qualification activities.
  • Develop or approve technical protocols, reports, engineering studies, acceptance criteria, statistical analyses, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure polymer-processing activities comply with applicable quality-system requirements, engineering standards, regulatory expectations, and internal procedures.
  • Support risk-management activities, including process FMEAs, design FMEAs, control plans, process-risk assessments, and technical investigations.
  • Partner with Quality Engineering to establish effective process controls and ensure sustained process capability.
  • Provide technical support during internal audits, external audits, regulatory inspections, and customer inquiries, as needed.

Manufacturing and Business Performance

  • Lead the resolution of complex or recurring molding process and/or tooling issues affecting safety, quality, delivery, capacity, cost, or customer service.
  • Apply structured problem-solving methods and advanced data analysis to identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Improve manufacturing performance through cycle-time reduction, scrap reduction, yield improvement, process-capability improvement, automation, tooling optimization, and material utilization.
  • Develop solutions that increase process reliability, reduce variation, and improve overall equipment and operational effectiveness.
  • Assess existing molding equipment, auxiliary systems, tooling, and processes to identify capability gaps, obsolescence risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Support capital-equipment selection, technical justification, supplier evaluation, installation, qualification, and production implementation.
  • Provide technical leadership for design changes, material changes, product transfers, process transfers, supplier transitions, capacity expansion, and manufacturing-network initiatives.
  • Develop business cases and recommendations supported by technical evidence, risk assessment, financial impact, and implementation requirements.

Technical Influence and Collaboration

  • Act as a technical consultant to engineering teams, operations leaders, project teams, and senior leadership.
  • Lead cross-functional technical initiatives that may span multiple products, departments, suppliers, or manufacturing locations.
  • Influence decisions where technical complexity, business risk, or organizational impact is significant.
  • Build effective partnerships with equipment manufacturers, toolmakers, resin suppliers, contract manufacturers, consultants, and other external technical resources.
  • Represent manufacturing and polymer-processing considerations in product, technology, and business-planning discussions.
  • Facilitate technical reviews and ensure decisions, actions, risks, and accountabilities are clearly documented.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical audiences at all levels of the organization.

Knowledge Development and Mentoring

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to engineers, technicians, molders, and other manufacturing professionals.
  • Build organizational capability by sharing specialized knowledge, developing technical training, and establishing repeatable engineering methods.
  • Review and provide guidance on the technical work of other engineers without serving as their direct manager.
  • Promote disciplined experimentation, fact-based decision making, continuous improvement, and strong engineering practices.
  • Maintain current knowledge of developments in polymer science, molding technology, manufacturing systems, medical-device requirements, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to the development of CONMED’s long-term polymer-processing and manufacturing-technology roadmap.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, or closely related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving injection molding, polymer processing, plastics manufacturing, tooling, or closely related manufacturing technologies.
  • 2 years of experience applying technical knowledge and expertise troubleshooting injection molded parts noncompliance opportunities to determine whether root cause is part design geometry, raw material, raw material handling, molding process, mold steel dimensions, mold steel wear, mold design conceptualization, molding cell selection, molding cell functional performance, part’s inspection method, inspection fixture, inspection equipment, parts conveying, parts packaging design, parts storing and/or part’s transit related.
  • 2 years of experience leading complex technical projects and influencing decisions across multiple functions. Experience developing or reviewing engineering protocols, validation documents, technical reports, specifications, risk assessments, and process documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or doctorate in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline.
  • Experience in a regulated medical-device, pharmaceutical, life-sciences, automotive, aerospace, or similarly controlled manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with injection molding of medical-device components or other high-precision, high-reliability products.
  • Working knowledge of applicable FDA quality-system requirements, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, good manufacturing practices, and process-validation expectations.
  • Expertise in one or more specialized processes, such as insert molding, overmolding, micro-molding, multi-shot molding, silicone molding, high-temperature materials, or bio-compatible polymers.
  • Experience with mold-flow simulation and analysis tools.
  • Experience with automation, in-mold sensing, process-monitoring systems, machine connectivity, or advanced manufacturing controls.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or structured problem-solving certification.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing transfers, supplier development, capacity expansion, or global operations.
  • Experience working with toolmakers, resin suppliers, equipment manufacturers, and contract manufacturers.
  • Experience with mold design conceptualization, mold manufacturing, mold functional performance testing and mold predictive and preventive maintenance programs.
  • Demonstrated expertise in injection molding process development, optimization, validation and troubleshooting assessment; and in mold design conceptualization, performance testing, plastic forming steel compliance, grooming activities, and troubleshooting assessment.
  • Advanced knowledge of thermoplastic materials, polymer behavior, resin handling, drying, rheology, shrinkage, warpage, degradation, and material-process interactions.
  • Demonstrated experience applying scientific molding principles, design of experiments, statistical analysis, process-capability methods, and structured root-cause analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently define problems, evaluate technical alternatives, and deliver sustainable solutions to highly complex engineering challenges.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and technical documentation skills.

Job Summary:

In this role, you will lead the technical evaluation, characterization, and qualification of raw materials used in medical devices, including polymers, elastomers, metals, coatings, and other functional materials. You will evaluate raw material testing specifications, review purchasing specifications, assess supplier documentation, and establish scientifically justified acceptance criteria to ensure materials meet product, quality, and regulatory requirements.

Working closely with R&D, analytical sciences, quality, procurement, supplier quality, and manufacturing teams, you will conduct material characterization, assess material variability, evaluate alternate materials and suppliers, and establish correlations between raw material properties and medical device performance. You will also support material qualification, change control, and investigations to ensure consistent material quality and reliable medical device manufacturing.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Evaluate and develop raw material testing specifications, including test parameters, analytical methods, sampling requirements, and acceptance criteria.
  • Review and optimize raw material purchasing specifications to ensure alignment with product requirements, supplier specifications, and internal quality standards.
  • Analyze supplier technical data sheets, Certificates of Analysis (CoAs), safety data sheets, and other relevant technical documentation to assess material compliance.
  • Characterize raw materials using appropriate analytical techniques, such as FTIR, DSC, TGA, GPC/SEC, rheology, moisture analysis, chromatography, and mechanical testing, as applicable.
  • Establish scientifically justified acceptance limits based on material properties, historical data, supplier capabilities, product requirements, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate new materials, alternate grades, and supplier changes through comparative analysis and material equivalence assessments.
  • Investigate material variability, out-of-specification results, contamination, and material-related manufacturing or product performance issues.
  • Support raw material qualification, supplier approval, incoming inspection optimization, change control, and nonconformance investigations.
  • Assess the impact of raw material properties on medical device functionality, processability, biocompatibility, sterilization compatibility, and product reliability, as applicable.
  • Collaborate with R&D, analytical, quality, procurement, and manufacturing teams to resolve material-related technical challenges.
  • Prepare material evaluation reports, specification justifications, qualification protocols, and technical documentation in accordance with applicable quality-system requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve raw material quality, strengthen supplier controls, and optimize material testing requirements.

Education

  • M.S. or M.Tech. in Materials Science and Engineering, Polymer Science, Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • A B.E./B.Tech. degree in a relevant discipline may also be considered with suitable industry experience.

Work Experience

  • 5–8 years of relevant experience in raw material characterization, analytical testing, material qualification, or specification development, preferably in the medical device, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or regulated manufacturing industry.
  • Hands-on experience evaluating raw material testing specifications, acceptance criteria, and purchasing specifications.
